title: ork status --summary: running, waiting on you, blocked, and next, in one view

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
*Proposed.* "What is running, what is left, how is it going" took four commands and a manual read on 2026-11-09: `ork status` (runs and open questions), `slicer list --pass v1.1`, `slicer status` (next and blocked), and the run records for per-role progress. Each source is right; none shows the whole picture, and a blocked slice is blocked on one of three things that look the same in the list: a slicer dependency, an owner question, or an owner action outside ork (S301 and the local launchers; S244 and the Grok matrix edit).

Slicer already provides the dependency view: `slicer status` prints Next, Progress and "S245 waits on S244" (checked 2026-11-09), so this slice does not recompute dependencies. It adds the parts only ork knows:
- Running: each live run with item, state, current role and vendor, round, and time in state (`engineRuns`, `internal/source/source.go`, and the `working: implementer round 1, 5m` line already in `ork show`).
- Needs you: open adj questions, open spec-check questions, awaiting-approval runs, paused runs, and human checks marked `later` (counts and the one command for each).
- Blocked: slicer's blocked list, plus the owner actions recorded as open (an item with the `needs-owner` flag, `ps.Held`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:403`).
- Next: slicer's next item and the next unblocked few by score, with a note for any that will raise spec questions.

Open questions:
- Q1 where. (a) `ork status --summary` for one project, default for the current project (recommended; plain text plus `--json`). (b) a new command `ork summary`. (c) a TUI view only.
- Q2 depth. (a) at most 5 lines per section with "+N more" (recommended). (b) unlimited.
- Q3 the "waiting on an owner action outside ork" source. (a) the `needs-owner` item flag only (recommended; exists today). (b) a free-text note convention.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- With one running run, one awaiting approval, one open spec question, one open adj question, one human check marked `later`, and a slicer item blocked by another, `ork status --summary` prints a Running section (item, state, role, round, time in state), a Needs you section (each with its command), a Blocked section (slicer dependency and owner-flag reasons, each named) and a Next section.
- Sections are capped at 5 lines with "+N more".
- An empty section prints `none`, not a blank.
- `--json` prints the same data with stable keys.
- Without a running daemon the command prints the error the other status commands print.
- No dependency edges are computed in ork: the blocked list is slicer's output (a fake slicer returns it).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add a `status.summary` daemon read (or build it in the CLI from `status` plus a `slicer status --json` call; prefer the CLI to keep the daemon surface small).
2. Format the four sections; reuse the status line helpers for the Running rows.
3. Add the flag and the usage line; docs and CHANGELOG, marked *proposed*.
